def brew_order(base, synergy):
    """
    A cauldron starts empty. There are n ingredients labeled 0..n-1
    (1 <= n <= 12), each of which must be added exactly once, one at a
    time, in some order you choose.

    base is a list of n integers. synergy is an n x n list of lists of
    integers with synergy[i][i] == 0 for every i. All values satisfy
    |value| <= 10**6 and may be negative.

    When ingredient j is added while the cauldron already contains the
    set S of previously added ingredients, the potency gained at that
    step is

        base[j] + sum(synergy[i][j] for i in S)

    i.e. synergy[i][j] is earned only when i was added strictly BEFORE
    j; synergy[j][i] is an independent (possibly different) value that
    applies to the opposite relative order. The total potency of an
    order is the sum of the n step gains.

    Return a tuple (best, order) where best is the maximum achievable
    total potency (an int) and order is the lexicographically smallest
    permutation of 0..n-1 (as a list of ints) whose total potency
    equals best.

    >>> brew_order([1, 1], [[0, 5], [2, 0]])
    (7, [0, 1])
    >>> brew_order([3, 3], [[0, 4], [4, 0]])
    (10, [0, 1])
    >>> brew_order([0, 0, 0], [[0, 1, 9], [8, 0, 1], [1, 1, 0]])
    (18, [1, 0, 2])
